chunks: From him, from one of our companions, from Al-Asamm, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Eat the endive, for there is no morning but that a drop from Paradise descends upon it. So when you eat it, do not shake it off.'
He said: And Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'My father (peace be upon him) forbade us from shaking it off whenever we ate it.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.الْهِنْدَبَاءَ: Endive, a type of leafy green vegetable

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of eating endive according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* underscores the medicinal and spiritual virtues of endive (*hindaba*), linking its daily consumption to divine sustenance through the metaphor of a 'drop from Paradise.' The instruction not to shake off the dew emphasizes the appreciation of natural blessings and reflects the practical health wisdom preserved in Shia hadith literature regarding dietary habits.
